Why 4 in 10 Indian children go to private schools
items.summary: Four in 10 Indian schoolchildren were enrolled in private unaided schools in 2025-26, up from 35.4 percent in 2018-19, according to Unified District Information System for Education ( UDISE+ ) data. Private-school enrolment increased by about 3 million in the past year, while government schools—where 48 percent of children are enrolled—saw their numbers decline by about 2.7 million. In 12 states and two Union territories (UTs), more than half the students went to private schools. Bihar, Goa and Jharkhand had less than 20 percent enrolment in private schools, while West Bengal had under 10 percent. Parents are increasingly choosing private schools at lower levels: 71 percent students in pre-primary or kindergarten and 40 percent in primary (grades I to V) were in private schools. In contrast, about 10 percent of students at the primary level were in government schools. Research studies show, and experts say, that perceptions of learning, affordability, school performance and availability of English-medium instruction affect parents’ choices. Choosing a private school also comes at a higher cost. Average annual education-related expenditure was Rs 28,693 per student in private school

The only other records of Demoiselle Crane sighting from Tamil Nadu comes from Vijayanarayanam Tank in Tirunelveli. items.title: Kolhapur circuit bench of Bombay High Court to get 75 acres, 495 permanent staff
items.summary: The Maharashtra Government has sanctioned 75 acres of land at Shenda Park in Kolhapur and created 495 permanent staff positions for the circuit bench of the Bombay High Court at Kolhapur. This announcement was made during the foundation day celebration of the Kolhapur bench which was established a year ago. Acting Chief Justice of Bombay High Court, Ravindra V Ghuge , highlighted the administrative push behind the land allocation. He recounted a conversation he had with Chief Minister (CM) Devendra Fadnavis during a high level meeting. “ I asked the CM ‘if slightly more land can be sanctioned for Kolhapur, this issue will be settled permanently, eliminating the need to request additional land in the future.' The Chief Minister showed great generosity. 75 acres of land has been officially transferred on paper to the Bench. Further, 495 permanent staff positions are being created specifically for the Kolhapur High Court Bench," the judge said.
